decisions.reason: As a core door-handle family with likely low carrying cost and strong fit to the firm's specification business, it should be kept, although after two years without a standout success signal the option is somewhat less protected than in 2024.

The mitred family still broadens the design offer for architects and planners, but another year without clear evidence of exceptional traction raises the chance of later portfolio rationalization while not yet justifying withdrawal.

This multifunctional handle remains strategically relevant to accessibility and system solutions, yet its more specialized use case means that by now management would expect clearer demand and therefore sees a materially higher withdrawal risk than for standard families.
The award-winning door and window handle collection has strong positive market and brand signals, so its option value remains high and the likelihood of discontinuation stays very low.

A finish variant is inexpensive to maintain and supports architecture-led specification choices, so it is still worth keeping unless sales data turn clearly weak, which implies only a modest withdrawal risk.
